blocks.prompt: 13 Find the general solution of the differential equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \cos^2\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) + \frac{y}{x}\).
blocks.explanation:
The right side contains \(x\) and \(y\) only through the ratio \(y/x\), so the equation is homogeneous (Section 4.2.2).
We must find the general solution, with one arbitrary constant.
Plan: put \(y = vx\), separate \(v\) and \(x\), integrate, then put back \(v = y/x\).
steps:
Given: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \cos^2(y/x) + y/x\).
To find: the general solution.
Method: Homogeneous equation: substitute \(y = vx\), so \(\frac{dy}{dx} = v + x\frac{dv}{dx}\). The equation then becomes separable in \(v\) and \(x\).

Substitute \(y = vx\)
\[v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \cos^2 v + v\]
Why: \(y/x = v\), and differentiating \(y = vx\) by the product rule gives \(\frac{dy}{dx} = v + x\frac{dv}{dx}\).

Cancel \(v\)
\[x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \cos^2 v\]
Why: \(v\) appears on both sides, so it cancels. This always happens when the right side is "\(v\) + something".

Separate the variables
\[\dfrac{dv}{\cos^2 v} = \dfrac{dx}{x}\]
\[\sec^2 v\,dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}\]
Why: all \(v\)-terms go with \(dv\), all \(x\)-terms with \(dx\) (we divide by \(\cos^2 v\), assuming \(\cos v \neq 0\)); \(1/\cos^2 v = \sec^2 v\).

Integrate both sides
\[\int \sec^2 v\,dv = \int \dfrac{dx}{x}\]
\[\tan v = \ln|x| + \ln|C|\]
\[\tan v = \ln|Cx|\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{dv}\tan v = \sec^2 v\) and \(\int \frac{1}{x}\,dx = \ln|x|\). Writing the constant as \(\ln|C|\) lets the two logarithms combine.

Put back \(v = y/x\)
\[\tan\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \ln|Cx|\]
Why: the answer must be in the original variables \(x\) and \(y\).

Check
Differentiate \(\tan(y/x) = \ln|Cx|\) with respect to \(x\):
\[\sec^2\!\left(\tfrac{y}{x}\right)\dfrac{xy' - y}{x^2} = \dfrac{1}{x}\]
\[xy' - y = x\cos^2\!\left(\tfrac{y}{x}\right)\]
Dividing by \(x\) gives back \(y' = \cos^2(y/x) + y/x\) \(\checkmark\)
Why: getting the given equation back confirms the solution.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints this answer as number 14, not 13. The Exercise 4.2 keys are numbered 2 to 29 for 25 questions (key 2 answers Question 1, and the extra keys 15, 19 and 27 match no printed question), so look for this answer under 14. The answer itself, \(\tan(y/x) = \ln|Cx|\), is correct.
